title: AIP-C01 Skill 1.5.4: Hybrid Search and Reranking
html:
AIP-C01 Skill 1.5.4: Hybrid Search and Reranking

A hands-on lab with keyword search, vector search, reciprocal rank fusion and a Bedrock reranker model. Task 1.5, post 4 of 7.

[IMAGE: cover-1-5-4.png — alt: "Skill 1.5.4: Hybrid search and reranking"]

AIP-C01 Hands-on Labs · Domain 1 · Task 1.5: Design retrieval mechanisms for FM augmentation · Post 4 of 7. Hands-on lab, about 25 minutes.

A customer types “Which blade fits my HT-650?”. To an embedding model, HT-650 is just a few characters that look a lot like HT-450 and HT-600. Vector search finds passages about blades and hedge trimmers, but not necessarily the one with that exact part number. Keyword search finds the exact code instantly, but fails on “Can I send back something I bought on clearance?”, where none of the words match the policy. Each method fails where the other succeeds. This skill is about combining them, then putting the best result first.

What AWS says

Skill 1.5.4: Create advanced search architectures to improve the relevance and accuracy of retrieved information for FM context (for example, by using OpenSearch for semantic search, hybrid search that combines keywords and vectors, Amazon Bedrock reranker models).

What it means in plain words

  • Semantic search: vector search; finds passages with similar meaning even when the words differ.
  • Hybrid search: run keyword search (BM25) and vector search together and fuse the two ranked lists.
  • Reranker models: a second model that reads the question and each candidate passage together and scores how well the passage answers it. Slower per passage, so it only reorders a short list.

[IMAGE: t1-5-4-pipeline.png — alt: "Retrieve broadly, then rerank: keyword search, vector search, fusion, rerank, top passages to the model"]

What we're going to do

  1. Run one question through four methods: keyword, vector, hybrid, and hybrid followed by a reranker.
  2. Try a part-number question and a paraphrased question.
  3. Compare all four methods across eleven test questions: where does the right passage land?

What you'll learn

  • Why keyword and vector search fail on different questions.
  • How reciprocal rank fusion combines lists whose scores aren't comparable.
  • How to call a Bedrock reranker model, and what it can and can't fix.
  • How to turn on hybrid search and reranking in Knowledge Bases and OpenSearch.

What you'll need

  • Time and cost: about 25 minutes, under US$0.05
  • Region: us-west-2 (Amazon Rerank 1.0 is offered in a few Regions, including us-west-2)
  • Access: Python 3.10+ with boto3; bedrock:InvokeModel on Titan Text Embeddings V2 and amazon.rerank-v1:0, and bedrock:Rerank
  • Files: github.com/prasanth2006z/aip-c01-labs, folder domain-1/task-1.5/skill-1.5.4-hybrid-rerank, plus the shared folder

The lab

Step 1: One question, four methods

pip install boto3
python hybrid_rerank.py search "Which blade fits my HT-650?"

Keyword search (BM25, in shared/search.py) puts the parts passage first, because ht-650 is a rare token that appears only there. Vector search may rank it lower, behind other passages about hedge trimmers. Compare the scores too: BM25 scores and cosine similarities are on completely different scales.

Step 2: A paraphrased question

python hybrid_rerank.py search "How long do I have to return a hedge trimmer?"

Now the strengths swap. Vector search understands that the garden equipment policy is about hedge trimmers and returns. Keyword search is distracted by every passage containing “return” or “hedge trimmer”, including the parts list.

Step 3: Fuse, then rerank

Because the scores aren't comparable, hybrid search fuses by rank instead, with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF):

def rrf(*result_lists, k=5, c=60):
    for results in result_lists:
        for rank, r in enumerate(results, 1):
            fused[r["id"]] += 1 / (c + rank)

A passage near the top of either list gets a good fused score; one near the top of both gets the best. Then the reranker reads the question with each of the eight fused candidates and reorders them:

agent_runtime.rerank(
    queries=[{"type": "TEXT", "textQuery": {"text": query}}],
    sources=[... one INLINE text document per candidate ...],
    rerankingConfiguration={"type": "BEDROCK_RERANKING_MODEL",
        "bedrockRerankingConfiguration": {"numberOfResults": 3,
            "modelConfiguration": {"modelArn": RERANK_ARN}}})

Step 4: Compare across all questions

python hybrid_rerank.py compare

The table shows, for each question and method, where the correct passage ranked (- means not in the top eight), and a final “ranked first” count. The pattern to look for:

  • Codes and IDs (HT-650 blade, BP-18-4Ah charge time): keyword wins, vector struggles.
  • Paraphrases (“send back something I bought on clearance”): vector wins, keyword struggles.
  • Hybrid gets the right passage into the list for both kinds, though not always first.
  • Hybrid + rerank usually moves it to first place.

A reranker can only reorder what retrieval found. If the right passage isn't among the candidates, reranking can't help: fix retrieval recall first.

In a knowledge base or OpenSearch

  • Bedrock Knowledge Bases: in Retrieve or RetrieveAndGenerate, set "overrideSearchType": "HYBRID" (supported on OpenSearch Serverless, Aurora PostgreSQL and some other stores, not on every store type) and add a rerankingConfiguration to vectorSearchConfiguration, with Amazon Rerank or Cohere Rerank.
  • OpenSearch: a hybrid query with a match clause and a knn or neural clause, plus a search pipeline with a normalisation processor that rescales and combines the scores.

Common pitfalls

  • Adding raw BM25 and cosine scores: they're on different scales. Fuse by rank or normalise first.
  • Raising k instead of reranking: more passages in the prompt adds noise and cost. Rerank a broad list down to a few.
  • Reranking thousands of passages: rerankers are slow per passage. Give them 20 to 50 candidates.
  • AccessDeniedException on rerank: you need both bedrock:Rerank and bedrock:InvokeModel on the reranker model.

Clean up

Nothing to delete.

What to remember

  • Keyword search finds exact terms (codes, names, IDs); vector search finds meaning. Hybrid gets both.
  • Fuse with reciprocal rank fusion or score normalisation, never raw scores.
  • Retrieve broadly (20 to 50), rerank, send the top 3 to 5 to the model.
  • Bedrock reranker models: Amazon Rerank and Cohere Rerank, via the Rerank API or a knowledge base rerankingConfiguration.
  • Knowledge Bases hybrid search: overrideSearchType: HYBRID, on supported vector stores.
  • A reranker can't add a passage that retrieval missed.

The exam scenarios for this skill are in post 7 of this task: Task 1.5 Exam Notes.
